hook: Ashtanga has problems. The worst? You won't stop talking about it.
draft_hook: Tight back, stiff legs? Ashtanga has problems. Here's why.
hook_change_reason: Kept 'Ashtanga has problems'. The video says it, so it is not an attack from outside: the voice opens with 'There's so many problems with Ashtanga yoga' (0.5-2.4 s, burned 'THERE'S SO MANY PROBLEMS WITH ASHTANGA YOGA'), closes with 'Ashtanga yoga comes with problems, big ones' (97-100 s), and the original caption's first line is 'There are so many problems with Ashtanga yoga'. It is the setup of a joke. Dropped 'Tight back, stiff legs?'. In the video these are what practice shows you about your body when you begin ('all the crap your body has been hiding from you: tight back, tight legs, weak arms', 6-12 s). Ashtanga does not cause them. Placed in front of 'Ashtanga has problems', it tells a stranger that Ashtanga gives you a tight back and stiff legs. That is the opposite of the video and plays on health fear. Dropped 'Here's why': the video is a list, not a reason. The new hook flips what a stranger expects (injury, too hard, too early) into the joke the video ends on: you love it too much. Backing: 'But the worst part, you start preaching ... telling your parents, your friends, even your dog how amazing Ashtanga is' (83.3-89.5 s), and the original caption: 'Nobody cares, but you won't stop.' 11 words, plain words, no emojis, no asana named. It also fits the habit direction, because the problem is that people don't quit.

caption:
Six problems with Ashtanga. (Yes, it's a joke.)

1. Your body stops hiding the truth: tight back, tight legs, weak arms.
2. Your old jeans stop fitting.
3. Food becomes a project. You're googling vegetarian spots and hunting for decent chai.
4. Your body wants to move. No more all-day Netflix on the couch.
5. Friends want late-night burgers and booze. You order the salad.
6. The worst one: you tell everyone, even your dog, how amazing Ashtanga is.

So yes, Ashtanga has its problems. Your new habit comes with all of them. Worth it?

Clips from our Mysore and led classes with @boonchutanti at the shala in Bangkok.

Want to try a class with us in Bangkok? Comment TRIAL and we'll message you.

#aybkk #ashtanga #ashtangabangkok #yogabangkok #bangkokyoga #ashtangaproblems #ashtangayoga #yogahumor
truth_notes: Video is 1:46.7, posted 16 Jan 2025 by @aybkk (1,003 likes and 63 comments when downloaded). Format: a man who appears to be Boonchu (black tee, please confirm) sits outdoors on a lawn in front of a modern house and trees. He holds a small notebook and pen, with a bamboo tumbler in front of him, and talks to camera in English. Class clips are cut in about every 2-4 s. It is a deadpan joke list; the original caption's hashtags include #goodlaughs and #ashtangaproblems. What he says (Whisper small, corrected with the burned captions, which follow the voice word for word): 'There's so many problems with Ashtanga yoga, honestly it's a serious subject, I really need to speak about it. First, when you begin, you start realizing all the crap your body has been hiding from you: tight back, tight legs, weak arms, belly so big it refuses to suck in, and your legs feel like they're made of concrete. Lovely. Your starting point is basically a mess. Then you practice for a while and what happens? You start losing weight. Sounds good, right? No. Now you've got to spend all your money on new clothes because your leg doesn't fill out your jeans, your belly is gone, and everything you own makes you look like a deflated balloon. That's problem No. 2. Then there's food: you can't just shovel anything into your face anymore ... what's good for your nice little new yoga body. Suddenly you're googling vegetarian spots, hunting down decent chai or coffee, becoming that picky person at dinner: "Oh, I don't eat that, that's bad for me." Who even are you anymore? Here's another one: your body gets more active ... you can't just lie down on the couch all day watching Netflix and inhaling chips and popcorn like the good old days. Now your body is like, hey, let's move, let's do something. It's exhausting. And let's not forget the social problems. Your family wants you to eat their fried garbage, your friends want late-night booze and burgers, and you're stuck there like, no thanks, I'll just have this salad. They look at you like you've joined a cult, and honestly they're not wrong. But the worst part: you start preaching ... telling your parents, your friends, even your dog how amazing Ashtanga is. You're basically a walking advert for yoga. Nobody asked, but here you are spreading the word like some kind of Ashtanga missionary. So yeah, Ashtanga yoga comes with problems, big ones. But hey, at least you have a better body, [unclear: burned 'BETTER' then 'LTH', Whisper heard 'with the help of'; probably 'better health'], and fewer friends to annoy you with your new habit. Win-win, right?' The original caption has the same six numbered problems: 1 body tells the truth (tight back, stiff legs, weak arms, belly), 2 losing weight costs money, 3 food becomes a project (vegetarian place with decent chai), 4 you can't just lie around (Netflix, chips, popcorn; your body wants to move), 5 social drama (fried food, late-night burgers and booze), 6 you turn into an Ashtanga preacher ('Nobody cares, but you won't stop'). It ends 'So yeah, Ashtanga yoga has its problems ... Worth it, right?' and 'Video from today mysore, Monday led primary and Saturday led intermediate with @boonchutanti'. Line backing. That is VINYASA' and 'Yoga is 99% practice 1% theory' (same 'BREATHING' wall that the #10 and #12 packages identify as the AYBKK shala), filmed in both daylight and evening light. The original caption names the classes but no city. bkk-api.js in this repo lists Monday Led Primary and Saturday Led Intermediate with Boonchu at the Bangkok shala. That is the 2026 timetable, so it supports the caption but does not prove where the Jan 2025 footage was shot. 'Mysore and led classes with @boonchutanti' follows the caption's 'mysore, Monday led primary and Saturday led intermediate with @boonchutanti'. The talking head is not at the shala. It was filmed outdoors on a lawn, and the place is not shown or named, so the caption does not say where it is. Left out of the caption on purpose: weight-loss wording, 'healthier/better health', 'cult', 'missionary', 'garbage'. CHECK (second review): two face descriptions in risk 1 were wrong and are fixed (t 11 is a student in an assisted backbend plus the assistant; t 92-95 is the packed room in upward dog, not a woman lying face up). The 'better health' words at 102-103 s are uncertain and are marked that way; the caption does not use them. Every caption line traces to both the video and the original caption. No numbers, quotes or claims were added. The CTA line is exact. 8 hashtags, including the 5 required ones; #ashtangaproblems is from the original. Hook placement was checked against fine frames at 4-6 fps from 0 to 55.2 s and a full mockup. risks: 1) STUDENT FACES: many students can be recognised in a sales post shown to strangers: t 10.5-13.4 (a student in a white top in an assisted backbend, face upside down and clear, plus the man assisting), t 16.0-16.4 (woman at the left edge), t 24.8-29.2 (man with raised arms, plus the room), t 53.8-55.3 (woman in a maroon top, close to the camera), t 57.3-59.2 (shirtless man), t 73.5-78.3 and 80.5-83.3 (packed room from above, several looking at the camera), t 84.8-88.2 (young man, close), t 91.6-95.5 (packed led class in upward dog, two women in front close to the camera with clear faces), t 100.3-101.5 (standing group). Boonchu confirms consent. 2) MUSIC MIXED WITH THE VOICE: a music bed (steady beat about 86 bpm, sustained notes, no sung words heard) starts about 2 s in and runs to the end under the voice, in one mixed audio track. It cannot be muted or swapped for library music without losing the talk. Title unknown. If Instagram flags it, the only choice is to keep the original audio or not post. 3) JOKE WORDS: the video says 'like you've joined a cult' (burned 'A CULT.' at 81.0-81.7 s), 'some kind of Ashtanga missionary' (burned 'MISSIONARY' at 96.2 s), 'your family wants you to eat their fried garbage' (burned 'FRIES' / 'GARBAGE' at 72.2-73.2 s), and 'refuses to suck in' (burned 'SUCK' alone at 14.0 s). This is humour, not religious conflict, and the caption leaves these words out. 'Cult' and 'missionary' touch religion, and calling family food garbage can read as rude, so keep this in mind before any China or Russia repost. 4) WEIGHT: the video jokes about losing weight and 'your belly is gone' (21.7-30 s), and caption line 2 ('Your old jeans stop fitting') hints at it. No number and no promise, but it is a body-change hint in a sales post. Cut line 2 if Boonchu prefers. 5) LENGTH: 1:46.7 is long for strangers, and the hook's payoff ('the worst part, you start preaching') arrives at 83.3 s. The list keeps moving, but many viewers will leave before that. 6) BURNED TEXT ERRORS: word-by-word captions show slips, each for about 0.2-0.5 s: 'WHEN YOU BEGINNER' (6.0-7.0 s, should be 'begin'), 'THAT REFUSE TO SUCK' (13.2-14.0 s, 'in' missing), 'FIGURE IT WHAT'S GOOD' (38.7-39.2 s, should be 'out'), 'SHIPS' (61.8 s, should be CHIPS), 'FRIES GARBAGE' (72.2-73.2 s, spoken 'fried garbage'), and the broken fragments 'LTH' (102.7 s, probably part of 'health') and 'FEW' / 'ER' (103.3-103.7 s, 'fewer' split). They cannot be fixed without the original edit project. None clash with the hook. 7) CAPTION ZONE: the burned captions sit at y ~976-1017, right at the top of Instagram's bottom caption and username area. Check in the app preview whether Instagram's overlay covers them. 8) HOOK TIME: the box shows only 0-52.6 s, not the whole video, because faces fill the top band from about 54 s. That differs from the whole-video habit, so Boonchu should OK it. 9) LOCATION: the class clips match the Bangkok shala (murals, plus a class list that matches the timetable in this repo), but the original caption names no city, so Boonchu should confirm 'at the shala in Bangkok'. The talking-head location (a lawn by a house) is unknown and not named. 10) SPEAKER: the original caption does not say who talks. He appears to be Boonchu, reading from his notebook. My caption does not name him as the speaker; it tags @boonchutanti only for the classes, as the original does. 11) Footage is from Jan 2025.
